title: An Embedded Feature Selection Framework for Control

problem.claim: Control applications need fewer sensors while maintaining optimal control performance to achieve robust, low-cost, and computation-efficient controllers.

gap.claim: Existing feature-selection solutions for typical machine learning are difficult to apply to control systems with changing dynamics.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes the Dual-world embedded Attentive Feature Selection framework for selecting relevant sensors under dynamic control.
The framework analyzes deep reinforcement learning responses in a real world and a virtual peer with twisted features to quantify feature importance for control.
The framework is evaluated on cylinder drag reduction and four OpenAI classical control cases.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On cylinder drag reduction, D-AFS finds an optimized five-probe layout with 18.7% drag reduction relative to a state-of-the-art solution using 151 probes and 49.2% relative to a five-probe layout designed by human experts.
Across four OpenAI classical control cases, D-AFS achieves sensor configurations that are the same as or better than the originally provided solutions.
The source code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reducing sensor requirements while preserving control performance is important for robust, low-cost, and computation-efficient controllers.
Existing machine-learning feature-selection solutions do not readily handle control with changing dynamics.
D-AFS selects relevant sensors using responses from real and virtual worlds with twisted features.
The method is evaluated on cylinder drag reduction and four OpenAI classical control cases.
The reported results show improved or comparable sensor configurations and substantial drag-reduction comparisons.

source_observation.claim: Comparing reinforcement-learning responses in a real environment and a virtual environment with altered features can support quantitative sensor-importance estimation.

interpretation.claim: A paired-world intervention may make feature relevance measurable in settings where system dynamics change.

application.claim: For dynamic control systems, evaluate sensor-selection candidates by contrasting policy responses under real and feature-perturbed virtual conditions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported control cases or how virtual peers are constructed.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the training procedure, feature-perturbation mechanism, or optimization objective in detail.
The abstract does not provide statistical uncertainty, computational costs, or independent verification of the reported results.
